title: How far may you drop for lateral relief from an unplayable ball?
question: Your ball is under a bush. You decide to declare it unplayable and take lateral relief. How far may you drop?
explanation: When taking lateral relief for an unplayable ball, you must drop the ball within two club-lengths of where the ball lies, no nearer the hole.

juniorVersion.title: How far can you drop your ball if you can't play it?
juniorVersion.question: Your ball is stuck under a bush and you can't hit it. If you choose to drop it to the side, how far are you allowed to move away from where it was?
juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball cannot be played and you want to drop it to the side (lateral relief), you are allowed to drop it within two club-lengths from where your ball was, but not closer to the hole.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: This means you move the ball sideways (to the side), not closer to the hole, when you can't play it.
The length of your golf club, used to measure how far you can drop your ball.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children how to lay two clubs down on the ground to measure two club-lengths from the ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think you can drop anywhere you want away from the bush.
Children may think you can drop closer to the hole.
Some may believe 'nearest point you can play' means you can pick any spot you like.
